_readme: Jetify – 2D wing/fin sections. Edit freely; reload the page (no code changes needed).
Each section has one or more data points at a chord Reynolds number Re. Between points the model
interpolates linearly in log10(Re); outside the range the nearest point is used (no extrapolation).
clAlpha_perRad = 2D lift-curve slope, cdMin = minimum section drag (per planform area), clMax = 2D max lift.
null for cdMin / clMax = use the environment values 'Fin profile drag CD0' / 'Fin CLmax'.
thickness_pct and kornKappa (default 0.87, supercritical 0.95) feed the Korn drag-divergence Mach number.
IMPORTANT: the values below are APPROXIMATE, literature-typical numbers entered from memory, not
digitised from the sources. Check each value against the cited source before using it to justify a design.
confidence: 'typical' = well-documented section, value should be within a few %; 'rough' = sparse data,
especially at low Re – treat as an order-of-magnitude placeholder.

sections.name: Ideal thin airfoil (2π)
sections.source: Thin-airfoil theory (Anderson, Fundamentals of Aerodynamics, ch. 4)
sections.note: Previous Jetify behaviour. CD0 and CLmax come from the environment inputs.

sections.name: NACA 0006
sections.source: Abbott & von Doenhoff, Theory of Wing Sections (1959), App. IV; low Re: UIUC LSATs / airfoiltools.com (XFOIL)
sections.note: Thin: sharp leading-edge stall at low Re.

sections.name: NACA 0009
sections.source: Abbott & von Doenhoff (1959), App. IV; low Re: UIUC LSATs / airfoiltools.com (XFOIL)

sections.name: NACA 0012
sections.source: Abbott & von Doenhoff (1959), App. IV; low Re: Sheldahl & Klimas, SAND80-2114 (1981)

sections.name: NACA 64A010
sections.source: Abbott & von Doenhoff (1959), App. IV (high Re); low Re: XFOIL estimate
sections.note: Laminar drag bucket only at high Re and smooth surface; at RC Re it behaves like a thin 4-digit.

sections.name: NACA 16-012
sections.source: Lindsey, Stevenson & Daley, NACA TN-1546 (1948); low Re: XFOIL estimate
sections.note: Flat pressure distribution – used for propellers/hydrofoils to delay cavitation.

sections.name: NACA 66-012
sections.source: Abbott & von Doenhoff (1959), App. IV (high Re); low Re: XFOIL estimate
sections.note: Max thickness ~45 % chord; marine use for cavitation resistance.

sections.name: NASA SC(2)-0010 (symmetric supercritical)
sections.source: Harris, NASA TP-2969 (1990) – coordinates; coefficients are rough estimates
sections.note: Benefit is transonic wave drag only (M ≈ 0.7–0.8); no advantage at RC or AUV speeds.
